spots.bio: Navala is a Ba Highlands village of over 200 thatched bures, one of the few in Fiji still fully traditional in architecture.
spots.notes: Wikipedia says a small charge is required for photography and entering the village; no amount sourced. Cost left null: needs the real adult fee. Bus link from Ba per Wikipedia. fiji.travel Navala page cited by Wikipedia ('Navala's Tribute to Tradition') not readable (403). Cost: about FJD 30 per person to enter and hire a guide (Fiji Pocket Guide); another guide says FJD 40 paid in cash on arrival. Plus a sevusevu gift; no entry on Sundays per a tour listing. Approximate.

spots.bio: Mount Tomanivi, formerly Mount Victoria, is Fiji's highest peak at 1,324 m, reached by a trail from Navai village.

spots.bio: Vanua Balavu is the main island of the Northern Lau Group, with hot springs, a reef system and Lomaloma as its main village.
spots.notes: Wikipedia: 53 sq km, airstrip, hot springs, extensive reef, Lomaloma copra port. Homestay/guesthouse and flight details in draft not confirmed by a source I read.

spots.bio: Qilaqila, the Bay of Islands, is a reef of islets off Vanua Balavu; visitors must do sevusevu and get village permission.
spots.notes: From Wikipedia Vanua Balavu: Qilaqila also known as Bay of Islands; owners are the mataqalis of Mavana Village; all visitors must do sevusevu and have permission from Daliconi Village elders. No fee sourced. Limestone cathedral cave and marine reserve in draft unsourced.
unverified: bio relies on Wikipedia statement of sevusevu/permission; no visitor source
spots.ticket_reason: No official site; permission via villages

spots.bio: Lakeba is the Lau Group's provincial capital island and home of the chiefly Vuanirewa clan, with Tongan-influenced culture.
spots.notes: Wikipedia: tourism is of lesser importance; served by Lakeba Airport; Tubou is capital village. Caves, hillforts and homestays in draft not sourced.
